claims.claim: An alleged optimum has a linear-time verifiable certificate, even for arbitrary signed entries.
claims.evidence: Let F_l be the maximum l-square sum. After O(mn) prefix-sum preprocessing, the verifier checks every L-square in O(mn) total and checks one supplied violating square for each l>L in O(q), where q=min(m,n). Acceptance proves F_L<=k and F_l>k for every l>L, exactly characterizing the optimum without assuming monotonicity. Conversely, every true optimum supplies these witnesses. The L=0 case is correctly handled by a vacuous feasibility check and witnesses for all positive lengths. This is O(mn) arithmetic/word operations and is unaffected by signed entries.
claims.witness: The generic certificate is L together with valid coordinates (r_l,c_l) satisfying sum(r_l,c_l,l)>k for every l>L.
claims.search_method: Direct soundness/completeness and complexity proof, supplemented by exhaustive arbitrary-precision checks on 106215 signed matrix/threshold instances, including every alleged L.

claims.claim: There is an exact output-sensitive search algorithm whose worst-case time is O(mn min(m,n)).
claims.evidence: Descending inspection returns the first feasible length, hence the exact maximum even when feasibility is nonmonotone. For m>=n=q and d=q-L, length q-t has (m-n+t+1)(t+1) placements, so the inspected placements are bounded by the stated sum for 0<=t<=d. Its expansion is O((m-n+1)(d+1)^2+(d+1)^3); preprocessing adds O(mn). For L=0 the actual last index is q-1, so including t=q only enlarges the bound. Since d<=q, the worst case is O(mnq), and fixed d gives O(mn). Transposition handles n>m.
claims.witness: The retained first violating placement at every tested infeasible length is also the certificate required by claim 0.
claims.search_method: Derived the placement count in both rectangular orientations and exhaustively compared the descending algorithm with brute force on 106215 signed instances.

claims.claim: Feasibility can alternate at every side length, and the natural no-revisit greedy extension is incorrect.
claims.evidence: In the stated n by n family, an even-length first-row interval sums to 0, while an odd-length interval sums to plus or minus 1 and the interval starting in column one sums to 1. Squares not meeting the first row sum to 0. Thus F_l=0 for even l and F_l=1 for odd l, yielding alternation at threshold 0. In the 2 by 3 example, the two side-2 sums are 1 and 4, while F_1=2. A scan that passes the first side-2 position, decreases to side 1 only at the second position, and never revisits the first position misses its entry 2 and can incorrectly return 1 rather than 0.
claims.witness: For alternation, A[1,j]=1,-1,1,-1,..., all other rows zero, and k=0. For greedy failure, A=[[2,1,1],[-3,1,1]] and k=1.
claims.search_method: Exact derivation plus arbitrary-precision checks for every length at n=1,...,32 and a direct trace of the 2 by 3 counterexample.

claims.claim: The O(mn) endpoint is achievable for two nontrivial signed separable classes: multiplicative rank one and additive separability.
claims.evidence: For A_ij=u_i v_j, every l-square sum is xy for independent row- and column-window sums x and y. The maximum over their Cartesian product is one of the four products of the two minima and maxima. With a nonzero pivot p=A_rc, the identity pA_ij=A_icA_rj recognizes rank one and gives each square sum as XY/p; every relevant numerator is exactly divisible by p, and evaluating all four quotients handles either sign of p. For A_ij=u_i+v_j, the maximum is l(max X_l+max Y_l), and A_ij=A_i1+A_1j-A_11 recognizes the class. Window extrema cost O(m+n) per length, and q(m+n)<=2mn.
claims.witness: Signed nontrivial examples include u=(2,-3), v=(-1,4) for multiplicative rank one and u=(2,-3), v=(-4,5) for additive separability.
claims.search_method: Direct algebraic proof plus exact testing of 28800 generated separable matrices and 31875 arbitrary matrices for both recognition identities.

claims.claim: A thresholded max-plus-convolution scan embeds exactly into matrices supported on one row.
claims.evidence: For l=B-t, each top-row window telescopes to p_{s+B-t}-p_s. Writing i=s and j=t-s, valid indices give C+x_i+y_j. If i>=N, the value is at most y_j+C-H<=-1; if j>=N, it is at most x_i-H<0. Valid values are at least C-2W=1, while squares below the supported row have sum 0. Therefore F_{B-t}=C+max_{i+j=t}(x_i+y_j) for every 0<=t<=2N-2. Feasibility at threshold C+K is exactly c_t<=K, and decreasing encoded lengths makes the largest feasible one correspond to the least such t. The three arbitrary middle prefix values are never window endpoints.
claims.witness: The stated construction with B=4N, C=2W+1, H=C+W+1, p_i=-x_i, and p_{B-j}=y_j+C realizes the embedding for every integer x,y.
claims.search_method: Checked all valid and invalid endpoint cases algebraically and exhaustively tested 7380 vector pairs, 99648 encoded lengths, multiple thresholds, and two radically different middle-prefix assignments using exact integers.

claims.claim: If integer bit lengths are unbounded and bit operations are charged, an O(mn) bound independent of bit length is impossible.
claims.evidence: On the 1 by 1 equality input a=k=2^(B-1), feasibility holds. For every lower bit r, changing only that bit of a to obtain 2^(B-1)+2^r makes feasibility fail while preserving bit length B. Along the equality execution, an exact algorithm in the explicit-binary bit-access model must therefore inspect every lower bit; otherwise an uninspected alternative is indistinguishable. This gives Omega(B) bit cost and excludes a bound O(mn)=O(1) independent of B. It is only an input-length obstruction and says nothing against O(mn) unit-cost arithmetic or bounded-word time.
claims.witness: For each B>=2, compare (a,k)=(2^(B-1),2^(B-1)) with a'=2^(B-1)+2^r for every 0<=r<B-1.
claims.search_method: Decision-tree adversary proof plus exact verification of 32640 same-length one-bit alternatives for B=2,...,256.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a general O(mn) algorithm on signed integer matrices or a matching impossibility result under an appropriate standard assumption. The draft establishes useful certificates, an O(mn min(m,n)) exact search, sharp failures of monotonicity, two O(mn) special classes, and an exact max-plus embedding. It does not give the requested general O(mn) bounded-word/unit-cost algorithm or a substantive conditional lower bound against one. The unbounded-bit 1 by 1 lower bound is a generic input-reading obstruction and is too model-mismatched to fully resolve the intended endpoint. The final writeup explicitly acknowledges this limitation, so claimed_resolution PARTIAL is accurate and not overclaimed.
